gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-hun: Raw and chaotic, Disorder spaces its oversized lowercase well apart, every stroke drawn like it came from a compass pencil. Noto Sans Old Hungarian is friendlier, with open counters.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-ita: Disorder's y has a tail as thick as its arm, and that unbroken line gives it a blunt, scrappy look. Noto Sans Old Italic keeps its lowercase tight to the capitals, so the pair's strongest quality is the jolt between them.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-nor: Loud, blunt and crowded with attitude. Disorder makes its diagonals as thick as its uprights, while Noto Sans Old North Arabian packs a dense, tall lowercase band with outward-pointing terminals.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-per: Bent tubing meets friendly roundness. The pair's strongest quality is how Disorder's same-gauge letters, bold and jagged, sit above Noto Sans Old Permic, whose rounded forms stay open to the side.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-sog: Noto Sans Old Sogdian has a tall x-height nearly reaching its capitals, with wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk. And Disorder, with its bent-paperclip strokes, earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-old-tur: Disorder runs one unmodulated line across every glyph, with spaced-out, oversized lowercase that looks raw and loud. Noto Sans Old Turkic then settles things with chunky, open-mouthed curves.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Rough-edged and loud, with a thick-only outline throughout. Noto Sans Oriya keeps its curve gaps generous and its small letters nearly capital height, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-osage: Noto Sans Osage fills the line with inflated lowercase bowls and sweeping curves that never close up. Disorder is best at flat, blunt shouting; Noto Sans Osage is best at easy, approachable reading.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Disorder's stroke thickness never varies, and its big lowercase stands well apart from its neighbors. Noto Sans Osmanya does the quiet work, with wide, easy s turns and lowercase oversized beside its capitals.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-: Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong reads in contemporary fashion, with a high-set x-height and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle. Disorder earns its keep big and short.
